reason: The text describes a clear conflict between the Israelites (regular people) and the Egyptian elite (Pharaoh and his government). The passage establishes how the Egyptians enslave the Israelites and subject them to harsh labor, causing them to cry out in suffering. God then commands Moses and Aaron to confront Pharaoh and demand the release of the Hebrew slaves. The narrative structure presents an oppressor-oppressed dynamic between the ruling Egyptian establishment and the enslaved Israelite population.
